purpose: Writing router: which written form answers this reader, checked how. Policy situation-declared-checklists (project-meta registry, Brian 2026-10-06). The agent declares yes/no facts and the medium through scripts/writing_record.py; code derives the route; the agent checks off that route's items with evidence.

media.web_page: A page in a browser: figures, tables and interactive pieces are all available.
media.document: A file or doc read as a whole: figures and tables, no interaction.
media.chat: Slack, Teams, Telegram or similar: text, at most one image or a short table.
media.email: An email: text, at most one image or a short table.
media.agent_reply: A reply or report from an agent to Brian in a session.

facts.is_message_to_brian: An agent's reply or report to Brian in a session.
facts.is_dloa: An Inside Success Daily Log of Accomplishments.
facts.is_job_application: A resume, CV, cover letter or job-application answer.
facts.is_chat_message: A Slack, Teams, Telegram or similar message, DM or thread reply.
facts.reader_performs_task: The reader arrives to carry out a task step by step.
facts.asks_for_approval_or_resources: The document asks the reader to approve, fund or staff something.
facts.reader_decides_from_this: A named reader must make a decision mainly from this document.
facts.reports_transferable_failure: The subject is a failure whose mechanism applies to work the reader did not write.
facts.central_claim_needs_argument: The subject is an idea or claim the reader must be convinced of; any artifact is evidence.
facts.subject_is_built_artifact: The subject is a tool, demo or system the author built, and the reader first asks what it does.

rep-considered.text: Each part was checked: would a figure, table or interactive piece answer the reader better than prose? Where yes, it went through Representation Router and its disposition is recorded.
Each part was checked: would a figure or table answer the reader better than prose? Where yes, it went through Representation Router and its disposition is recorded.
A short table or one image is used where it beats prose; otherwise plain text.

A table is used where it beats prose; a page is linked instead when the answer needs a figure or interaction.

message_to_brian.name: Reply or report to Brian
message_to_brian.governed_by: ~/code/AGENTS.md: 'Persist and close' and the closing-field format

mb-answer-first.text: If Brian asked a question, the Answer comes first, in one to three sentences.

mb-lead-with-change.text: Leads with what changed, why it matters and what he can do next; jargon translated.

mb-one-request.text: Every request to Brian is in Need anything from human, standalone, and there is at most one.

mb-verified.text: Every claim under Done has a check under Verification that actually ran.

dloa-system-named.text: Every bullet names the system or project, not only the tool.

dloa-before-after.text: Every process verb has a concrete before and after.

dloa-no-unearned-adoption.text: No adoption or use is claimed for something only built.

dloa-tests-say-what.text: Every test or validation says what it confirmed.

dloa-no-padding.text: No bullet could be cut without losing information.

job-target-grounded.text: The exact role, employer and location come from the live posting.

job-work-record.text: Claims use the work record's resume_safe wording and obey its restrictions.

job-fit-first.text: The most relevant experience for the posting leads.

job-screened.text: Every outward line was screened for private or employer-internal detail.

job-read-back.text: The saved final artifact was read back: names, dates, links.

chat-lead-with-ask.text: If it wants something, the first sentence is the ask and the second is one sentence of why.

chat-no-announcing.text: No sentence describes the message instead of being it; signposting under about one per 1k words.

chat-only-asked.text: Answers only what was asked; no diagnosis of why the reader is stuck (branches instead).

chat-references.text: Every named artifact carries its exact locator inline.

chat-approved.text: Brian approved this exact content in the same conversation before sending.

email.name: Email
email.governed_by: write-slack skill (rules plus the Email section) and project-meta docs/ops/OUTBOUND_EMAIL_POLICY.md

email-frame.text: Opens 'Hello <first name>,' and closes 'Best,' with the sender's name; normal capitalization.

email-lead-with-ask.text: The first body sentence is the ask or the point, then one sentence of why.

email-subject.text: The subject names the ask or topic plainly.

email-slack-rules.text: No announcing sentences, only what was asked, exact references inline.

email-approved.text: Brian approved this exact content in the same conversation, per the outbound email policy.

d-steps-ordered.text: Steps are in order and each can be checked on its own.

d-commands-run.text: Every command shown runs as written.

d-failure-named.text: Each non-obvious failure mode is named where it can happen.

p-ask-first.text: The ask (what, how much, by when) is in the first paragraph.

p-problem-evidence.text: The problem is shown with evidence, not asserted.

p-cost-risk.text: Cost and the main risk are stated, with what happens if declined.

decision_brief.name: Decision brief (BLUF)
decision_brief.governed_by: ~/code/AGENTS.md 'Decision' format in Need anything from human

b-recommendation-first.text: The recommendation is the first sentence.

b-alternatives.text: Real alternatives are named with their tradeoffs.

b-confidence-impact.text: Confidence and the impact of being wrong are stated.

c-symptom-mechanism.text: Symptom, then mechanism, in that order.

c-conditions-early.text: The conditions that generalise it come early, not in a closing section.

c-cost.text: What the pattern costs is stated.

arg-order.text: The piece moves structure, then mechanism, then constraints, then implications.

arg-one-step.text: Each paragraph takes one inferential step.

arg-concrete.text: Never more than two abstract paragraphs in a row without the example.

a-real-output.text: Input, then output shown as a real artifact.

a-distinguishing.text: The distinguishing property and why the usual approach cannot do it, before the halfway point.

a-absences.text: What it deliberately does not do, stated as decisions with reasons.
